purpose: ASVS V1.5.3 had no decision. It asks that different parsers used for the same data type parse consistently, naming URI parsing divergence as the way it is exploited. A URL has one parser on this platform - the WHATWG one - and it is what the browser, undici and Node use when a value is finally resolved. The public AI-grounding source boundary had a second, hand-written one, and the two did not agree.
requiredInvariants: The divergence is measured and reproducible, not argued. With the real PRIVATE_PUBLIC_SOURCE pattern, five hrefs passed every string check and resolve outside the public contour: a dot, a tab and a dot carry no literal .. for includes('..') and are exactly .. for the WHATWG parser, which strips tab, line feed and carriage return before parsing. /platform-v7/.<TAB>./staff resolves to /staff and /platform-v7/.<TAB>./admin/users to /admin/users.

I got it wrong first and the probe corrected me. My initial run showed the bypasses rejected, because I had approximated PRIVATE_PUBLIC_SOURCE with an unanchored pattern that caught them by accident. The real one is anchored at ^/platform-v7/, so a path beginning /platform-v7/. is not a private segment and passes. The result only holds with the pattern the code actually uses.
Reachability was checked, not assumed: the href is rendered as <a href={href}> in PublicPlatformAssistant.tsx, so the browser's URL parser is the second parser in the pair.

The impact is bounded honestly. The destinations reached this way are themselves authenticated, so an anonymous visitor following such a link is refused. What fails is the contour boundary this check exists to enforce - a model-supplied citation could present a link into the private contour as an approved public source.

Closed by removing the second parser, not by improving the string test. publicPlatformSourcePath resolves with new URL against an unreachable .invalid base - the same device apps/web/lib/safe-redirect.ts already uses - refuses a change of origin or any credentials, and applies the contour rules to resolved.pathname.
The resolved form is what is returned and stored. Keeping the raw string would put the characters the parser reinterprets back into circulation even after the check passed.
The rule was duplicated in two files with two copies of the same constant; there is now one definition. Both call sites were rewired and 188 ai-insights tests pass unchanged.
The guard was shown to catch the original defect, not just an invented one: reintroducing the includes() check into the real service file makes it exit 1 naming both idioms.
No production, REG.RU, DNS or database mutation. No registration business logic, 1C, marketing or presentation change.
acceptance: node scripts/security/verify-parser-consistency.mjs exits 0 over 2155 files: zero hand-written URL tests, zero legacy node:url parsers.
jest src/modules/ai-insights: 14 suites, 188 tests, all passing - unchanged by the rewiring.
ASVS V1.5.3 moves NOT_ASSESSED to PASS: PASS 129 to 130, NOT_ASSESSED 39 to 38, FAIL and NOT_APPLICABLE unchanged, rejected decisions back to the single pre-existing V8.2.4.
Revocable: judging the raw string instead of the resolved path rejects V1.5.3 and fails four unit tests.
Six negative mutations each fail a named test or make the guard exit 1.
